question: hollow's undeclared tail: do the changed files come from the ticket's OWN commits (subject starts with <ticket id>) between pre-build and HEAD, or from the whole <pre-build>..HEAD diff as D2 says — accepting that test_hollow's live tooth 5 then measures 239 files and must loosen to seen ⊇ declared?
why_it_blocks: D2 (rehearsed clean) widens hollow's subject set to writes_to UNION git diff <pre-build>..HEAD. Built and measured 2026-09-18: on the fixture it reads exactly as cast (proof green twice bare). But the live tooth test_hollow.py:test_the_live_run_reads_every_writes_to_file... measures 9579a6f9cec6 (BUILDME 2026-09-07) on every seal, and its diff to HEAD is now 693 files, 239 of them measurable, against 10 declared — hours of proof runs per seal instead of ~250s, and the tooth's invariant seen == set(declared_files) reds deterministically. The same holds for any hollow re-run taken after other builds land. Two honest shapes and the choice is which files count as 'the build': (b) narrows 'changed' to the files touched by commits whose subject starts with the ticket id (the commit convention here), between pre-build and HEAD — cheap, precise, but leans on a convention; (c) keeps <commit>..HEAD as cast and loosens tooth 5 to seen ⊇ declared, accepting that a late hollow re-run measures the repo's drift. Either changes D2/D11 or test_hollow.py, so it is not mine to pick.
